items.title: DeFranco Buddy — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: Johnny played a long solo and I was so impressed, that kind of tipped me over into the area of jazz. I wanted to be a jazz clarinetist from that point on.

ctx.x: So he was one of the people kind of directing you to those performers.

Oh yeah, yeah. And then in the Earl Theatre they had these stage shows. Four and five shows a day. Big bands were coming through, and they’d have a big band and a movie. The big band for an hour and then they’d run a movie and a newsreel, and then the band would come play another show. I remember listening to Tommy Dorsey, watching and listening to Tommy Dorsey’s band. He featured a clarinetist, Johnny Mintz. Johnny played a long solo and I was so impressed, that kind of tipped me over into the area of jazz. I…
So how old were you when you heard Johnny Mintz? And that was live, that was a live performance.
